# Jubilees Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram Confronts Idolatry; Abram's Night Prayer; God Calls Abram; Journey Begins

---

**12:1** In the sixth week, seventh year, Abram went to his father Terah and said: "Father —"

**12:2** "What?" Terah answered. Abram said: "What exactly do we get from these idols you worship and bow down to? What help? What benefit?"

**12:3** "There's no spirit in any of them. They're silent objects — they confuse the people who trust them. Stop worshipping them."

**12:4** "Worship the God of heaven — the one who sends rain and dew on the earth, who does everything on the earth, who created everything by his word. All life comes from his presence."

**12:5** "Why bow down to things with no spirit? They're handmade. You carry them around on your shoulders and get nothing from them. They embarrass the people who make them and they delude the people who worship them."

**12:6** "Stop."

**12:7** His father sighed: "I know all this, son. But what am I supposed to do? These people have bound me to serve them."

**12:8** "If I tell them the truth, they'll kill me. They're too devoted to these things — their hearts are wrapped around them."

**12:9** "Stay quiet, son, or they'll kill you too."

**12:10** Abram tried the same argument on his brother Nahor, but Nahor got angry and refused to listen. His heart was fully committed to the idols.

**12:11** That night Abram got up and set the idol-house on fire. Everything inside burned. No one knew.

**12:12** When the people woke up and saw the fire, they rushed to rescue their gods.

**12:13** Haran ran in first — but the fire caught him and he burned to death, dying in Ur of the Chaldees before his own father. Terah buried him there.

**12:14** After that, Terah left Ur of the Chaldees with his sons, heading for Lebanon and Canaan. They stopped and settled in Haran, and Abram stayed with his father there for fourteen years.

**12:15** In the forty-first jubilee, third year of the first week, Abram came back to his father's house. Nahor was still there; Haran was dead.

**12:16** In the sixth year of the second week of the forty-first jubilee, Abram sat up alone all night, watching the stars from dusk to dawn, trying to read what the coming year's weather would bring.

**12:17** And then a thought broke through: "All of this — the stars, the moon, the sun — all of it is in God's hands. So why am I studying it?"

**12:18** "If God wants it to rain, it rains — morning or evening. If he doesn't, it doesn't. Everything is his to decide."

**12:19** He prayed right then: "My God — God Most High — you alone are my God. I have chosen you and your sovereignty. You created everything; everything that exists is your work."

**12:20** "Rescue me from the power of the evil spirits who control what people think and feel. Don't let them drag me away from you, my God."

**12:21** "Root me and my children in you forever — keep us from drifting, from now until the end."

**12:22** He sat there thinking: "Should I go back to Ur, where people are asking me to come back? Or should I stay here?"

**12:23** "The right path is open before you. Guide your servant's hands to walk it. Don't let my own confused heart lead me astray, O God."

**12:24** He finished praying — and the word of the LORD came to him through me, the angel, saying: "Leave your country, your family, your father's house, and go to a land I will show you. I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make your name famous, and you will be a blessing in the earth. Every family on earth will be blessed through you."

**12:25** "I will watch over all your descendants under the sun. Your descendants will be as countless as the sand on the seashore, and I will give them a great land to be their inheritance forever."

**12:26** Abram got up, took Sarai his wife and his nephew Lot son of Haran, and set off for Canaan. He came into the land of Asshur, made his way to Shechem, and camped near a great oak tree.

**12:27** He looked around: the land was beautiful from end to end — from the entrance of Hamath all the way to that oak.

**12:28** The LORD said to him: "This land — to you and your descendants, I give it."

**12:29** He built an altar on the spot and offered a burnt offering to the LORD who had appeared to him.

**12:30** Then he moved on to the hill country between Bethel to the west and Ai to the east, and pitched camp.

**12:31** The land spread out beautifully in all directions — lush with every kind of growth: grapevines, fig trees, pomegranates, oaks, evergreens, terebinths, olive trees, cedars, cypresses, date palms. Water ran in the mountains.

**12:32** He praised the LORD who had brought him out of Ur and guided him safely to this place.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Abram's night-astronomy scene (vv.16-18) rendered to make the intellectual breakthrough vivid. The divine call (v.24) explicitly comes "through me, the angel" — Jubilees' angelic narrator identifies himself. "Fourteen years" (v.14) renders "two weeks of years" transparently.*
